title: How to Choose the Right Trademark Class for Coir Products in Alappuzha
metaTitle: Choosing Coir Trademark Classes in Alappuzha | BRNDNUR Guide
metaDescription: Detailed classification guide for Alappuzha coir manufacturers. Map doormats, coco peat, rubberized mattresses, and geotextiles to Classes 27, 20, 1, and 19.
intendedAudience: Coir factory proprietors, mat exporters, coco-peat substrate processors, and natural fiber product innovators in Alappuzha district.
quickAnswer: Coir manufacturers in Alappuzha must classify their goods precisely under the international Nice Classification: Class 27 for finished doormats, runners, and floor rugs; Class 20 for rubberized coir mattresses and composite furniture; Class 1 for coco peat and horticultural growing media; and Class 19 or 22 for geotextiles and raw fiber ropes. Selecting the wrong class leaves commercial product lines unprotected against competitors.

h2Sections.h2: The Evolution of Alappuzha’s Coir Industry
content: Alappuzha has long served as the traditional center of global coir manufacturing, celebrated for turning raw coconut husk fiber into durable, eco-friendly consumer and industrial products. However, the modern coir sector is far more diverse than traditional hand-woven doormats.

Local enterprises now manufacture automated tufted PVC mats, rubberized ergonomic mattresses, horticultural coco-peat blocks for export to desert agriculture, and heavy-duty geotextile grids used in highway stabilization. Because each product category serves a distinct functional purpose, filing a trademark under a single generic class is one of the most common legal mistakes made by Alappuzha exporters.

callout.title: Classification Dictates Legal Scope
callout.text: Under the Trade Marks Act, 1999, registration in Class 27 (floor mats) gives zero statutory authority to stop a competitor from selling coco-peat compost or mattresses under your brand name in Class 1 or Class 20.

h2Sections.h2: Comprehensive Class Mapping for Coir Product Lines
content: Use this definitive classification roadmap to identify every Nice class relevant to your manufacturing operations in Alappuzha:
checklist: Class 27 (Finished Floor Coverings): Tufted coir doormats, bleached and printed coir rolls, rubber-molded welcome mats, handloom runners, and non-textile floor rugs.
Class 20 (Furniture, Bedding & Mattresses): Rubberized coir mattresses, orthopaedic mattress cores, coir composite building boards, and decorative cushions.
Class 1 (Horticulture & Agricultural Media): Washed and unwashed coco peat blocks, coir pith compost, organic soil conditioners, and plant propagation discs.
Class 22 (Raw Fibers & Cordage): Raw white and brown coconut fibers, coir yarn, curling ropes, and untwisted natural packaging fiber.
Class 19 / 24 (Civil Engineering Geotextiles): Woven and non-woven coir geotextile blankets for riverbank erosion control and roadbed reinforcement.

h2Sections.h2: Classification Decision Matrix for Alappuzha Manufacturers
content: Compare the statutory scope and commercial applications across the core coir classes:

rows: Direct imitation by retail home-store competitors.
Exporters losing brand identity on Amazon horticulture portals.
Coir sheets bound with natural latex
Rival mattress makers confusing retail buyers.

h2Sections.h2: Step-by-Step Filing Strategy for Coir Brand Owners
content: Execute this 4-step intellectual property protocol to secure multi-class protection efficiently:

First, perform a clearance search across Classes 27, 20, and 1 on the IP India database. Second, obtain an Udyam MSME certificate to claim the 50% government fee concession (paying ₹4,500 per class instead of ₹9,000). Third, file Form TM-A with Chennai Registry, submitting clean product specifications that clearly describe your actual finished goods rather than generic class headings.
checklist: 1. Multi-Class Clearance: Search exact and phonetic marks across target and allied classes.
2. Coir Board Integration: Align your brand name with your Coir Board Registration-cum-Membership Certificate (RCMC).
3. MSME Fee Subsidy: Save ₹4,500 per class using your valid Udyam registration.
4. Export Priority: Prepare Madrid Protocol international filings within 6 months of domestic filing.

faqs.question: Can I file a single trademark application covering both coir mats (Class 27) and mattresses (Class 20)?
faqs.answer: Yes. You can file a Multi-Class Application on Form TM-A covering multiple classes under a single application number. However, government statutory fees are calculated per class (₹4,500 per class for MSMEs, so ₹9,000 for two classes).

faqs.question: Does the Alleppey Coir GI Tag protect my private brand name?
faqs.answer: No. The Geographical Indication (GI) tag protects the authentic geographic origin of coir products produced in the Alappuzha region. It does not confer proprietary rights over your private commercial brand name or logo.
